However, the example displays $f_{12}$ as a free entry, and solving the defining equation $aZN^T+bNZ+NZN^T=0$ does not force this entry to vanish. Thus the claimed zero pattern for off-diagonal blocks of $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$ is false.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Case 2. $\lambda_j\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\lambda_j|=1$, $j=l_1+1,\ldots,r$. Clearly, there exists an unitary matrix $Q_j\in\mathbb{C}^{n_j\times n_j}$ such that $S_j=Q_j\Sigma_jQ_j^H$

issues.failure_explanation: For $|\lambda_j|=1$, the Jordan block $J_j$ in Case 2 has size $2n_j$ (two identical blocks $\lambda_j I_{n_j}$). Therefore the corresponding block of $\Gamma$ must also be $2n_j\times 2n_j$. The theorem states that $E_j$ has order $n_j\times n_j$, which cannot fill that block. Consequently, the displayed diagonal matrix for $\Gamma$ has total size less than $2n$ unless $l_1=r$. The proof's Case 2 likewise treats the block as an $n_j\times n_j$ matrix, so the argument does not establish the stated result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this section, we always assume that $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\Lambda_2^{-\star})=\emptyset$, $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\tilde{\Lambda}_1)=\emptyset$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof relies on Theorem \ref{main-thm}, which requires the updated pair $[\tilde{X};\tilde{X}\tilde{\Lambda}]$ to be nonsingular. The theorem only assumes $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\Lambda_2^{-\star})=\emptyset$ and $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\tilde{\Lambda}_1)=\emptyset$, but not that $\tilde{\Lambda}_1$ is disjoint from the remaining spectrum in the needed sense. The proof then sets $\tilde{X}_1=X_1\Phi$ without verifying the required nonsingularity. A concrete counterexample: take $n=2$, $p=2$, $\Lambda_1=\mathrm{diag}(2,1/2)$, $\Lambda_2=\mathrm{diag}(3,1/3)$, $\tilde{\Lambda}_1=\Lambda_2$, $X_1=X_2=I$, $\Gamma_1=\begin{bmatrix}0&b\\-b&0\end{bmatrix}$, $\Gamma_2=-\Gamma_1$, $\Phi=I$, and $\tilde{\Gamma}_1=\Gamma_1$. Then all stated assumptions hold, but $\tilde{A}^{-1}=\tilde{X}_1\tilde{\Lambda}_1\tilde{\Gamma}_1\tilde{X}_1^{\star}+X_2\Lambda_2\Gamma_2X_2^{\star}=\Lambda_2\Gamma_1+\Lambda_2(-\Gamma_1)=0$, so $\tilde{A}$ is undefined.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis ensuring the updated standard pair is nonsingular, e.g. $\sigma(\tilde{\Lambda}_1)\cap\sigma(\Lambda_2^{-\star})=\emptyset$ (or directly that $[\tilde{X};\tilde{X}\tilde{\Lambda}]$ is nonsingular), and verify it in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue embedding theorem and its no-spill-over guarantee fail when the new eigenvalues overlap with the remaining ones. The updated matrices may not be well-defined, so the theorem is false as stated.
issues.title: EEP theorem missing nonsingularity condition for updated standard pair
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated, but a standard disjointness condition restores a comparable result without requiring a new global proof architecture.
